newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-SIMPSON TAKES HAWAII GOLF LEAD AFTER SECOND ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SIMPSON TAKES HAWAII GOLF LEAD AFTER SECOND ROUND.

text.p: Scott Simpson shot a 66 to go with his opening-round 65 to take a two-stroke lead at the $1.2 million United Hawaiian Open on Friday.
In second place are Pete Jordan, who shot a two-under-par 70 at Waialae C.C., and Ed Dougherty, who had a second round 69.
Four players are next at 10 under par, including first round leader Mike Reid, who followed up his 62 with a 72 on Friday, and British Open champion Tom Lehman, who shot a 69.
Simpson had one bogey in his 66, and made three tap-ins among his seven birdies.
"I'm thrilled to be here, in the lead or near it," Simpson said. "It's nice to see my game coming together. I've worked extra hard on it. Also, it's great to do it with my all-star caddie."
Simpson's 14 year-old daughter Brea is carrying his bag this week.
"She wasn't too interested until I told her I'd pay her. It's been a lot of fun, though I have to be on my best behaviour this week. No throwing a club at my caddie this week."
The extra hard work is the result of a 1996 season which started well, with four top 10s, and then finished poorly.
This is the last year of his 10-year exemption for winning the 1987 U.S. Open, a deadline that gave him the motivation he needed to get back to work on his game.
Jordan had four birdies and two bogeys in his round on Friday, saying the difference between that and his opening 64 was the increased wind on Friday afternoon.

Dougherty's five birdie, two bogey for a 69 was one of the best scores of the afternoon. Dougherty said he was happy to be contending, but even more pleased to have made the cut, the first time in more than a year.
